newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks slip on blue-chip profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks slip on blue-chip profit-taking.

text.p: Caracas stocks slipped as investors took profits on Venezuelan blue-chips that rose to record-breaking levels in the past three sessions, brokers said.
"Share prices have risen so abruptly recently that profit- taking was inevitable," said Activalores broker Gonzalo Alonso.
The sell-off pushed the market's 19-share index down 0.30 percent to close at 4,85.21 points in trade volume that approached the year's record.
Over 58 million shares traded to a total value of 16 billion bolivars ($34 million).
That compares to Tuesday's trade volume of 17 million shares worth 3.3 billion bolivars.
"Activity was really high. That's a good indicator of sustained interest in Venezuela despite today's weaker market," said one broker.

Among traded issues, 17 rose, ten fell and ten closed flat with blue-chips heading the dip. Electricidad de Caracas lost 3.00 bolivars to close at 426.00, Sivensa dropped 2.00 bolivars to close 305.00 and Mavesa slipped 0.50 bolivars to end at 127.50.
